findings.evidence: "Specific and scannable (5-8 words ideal)", "Bullets for multiple points (3-5 max)", "One topic per email", plus the tone-by-audience table
findings.fix: Cut generic email-writing advice the model already knows (lead with the ask, short paragraphs, tone by audience). Keep only team-specific conventions the model could not guess, such as required subject tags, house style and sign-off rules.

findings.evidence: Step 2 "Use the What-Why-How structure" followed by generic bullets ("Provide necessary background")
findings.fix: Replace the generic framework with decision guidance, for example how to handle an escalation versus a request, or what to check before choosing a CTA. Add a pre-draft check such as "What single action should the reader take, and by when?"

findings.evidence: "Anti-Patterns to Avoid": "Wall of text without structure", "Over-apologizing or excessive hedging", "CC'ing unnecessarily"
findings.fix: Turn each item into a specific NEVER with a reason and a bad-to-good rewrite. Add environment-specific gotchas, such as never inventing names, dates or commitments the user did not supply, and flagging missing facts instead of guessing.

findings.evidence: description: Draft a professional email using the What-Why-How framework. Use when you need to compose emails to colleagues, stakeholders, or leadership.
findings.fix: Draft or refine a professional email (subject line, body, call-to-action) using the What-Why-How framework. Use when the user asks to write, draft, reply to, rewrite or tighten an email to a colleague, stakeholder, manager or customer, even if they do not say 'What-Why-How'. Not for Slack/chat messages or long documents.

findings.evidence: Step 5 offers four equal refinement options (tone, length, jargon, format) and Step 1 asks three mandatory questions as menus
findings.fix: Pick defaults (infer audience, purpose and urgency from $ARGUMENTS and ask only about what is missing) and offer one or two refinements instead of a four-way menu.

findings.evidence: No commands/evals/compose-email.json exists; commands/evals/ holds only explain-pr-changes.json and its fixtures
findings.fix: Add commands/evals/compose-email.json with 3 prompts and verifiable assertions: empty arguments (the command asks the 3 questions), a pasted draft to refine, and an urgent escalation. Assert that the subject carries an action tag, the opening states the ask, and no throat-clearing appears.

findings.evidence: Examples call "/soft-skills:draft-email" while the file is compose-email.md and the heading is "Draft Professional Email"
findings.fix: Make the example invocations match the real command name (/compose-email) and the namespace it ships under.

findings.evidence: Step 4 template has only a subject and body, but "Output" requires "Subject line with rationale" and "WHAT/WHY/HOW sections labeled"; Step 1 says "empty or insufficient" without defining it and does not say what to do with a pasted draft or an unanswered question
findings.fix: Reconcile Step 4 with the Output section (decide whether labels and rationale are shown). Define "insufficient", and add a branch: if $ARGUMENTS is a draft, refine it and ask only for missing facts. If a question goes unanswered, state the assumption and proceed.
